what: Dozens of sticker images on both sides of the Hero pop out from opacity 0 · 40px down · scale 0 with a spring (mass 4 · stiffness 800 · damping 80, about .69s), starting after .2s at .05s intervals with the back ones first. Each then floats with its own random tempo (2~3s, delayed 0~1s), swinging tilt −2~2° and vertical −2~5px. Dragging a sticker stretches it like a rubber band by only .1 of the hand’s movement, and on release it snaps back into place with a spring (stiffness 600 · damping 20).

options.spring: Spring mass, stiffness, damping on entry — default 4,800,80 (original phone-screen version is 4,800,60)
options.back: Spring mass, stiffness and damping on release — default 1,600,20
options.y: Distance to rise from below on entering (px · viewBox units), default 40
options.delay: Delay until the first sticker (sec), default .2
options.order: With forward, it starts from the first item, by default from the last (original staggerDirection −1)
options.rot: Tilt range while floating (deg) — end value is ±rot × random, default 2 (phone original 6)
options.bob: Up and down range while floating — default 2,5 (phone version original 5,5)
options.beat: Minimum length of one float (s), default 2 (phone version original 1)
options.jitter: Random range added to the float duration (seconds), default 1 (original phone version 2)
options.elastic: Ratio that follows the hand when dragging, default .1
options.drag: If false, dragging is off (always off on devices without touch input)
options.per: With parent, each parent group wrapping the stickers is delayed separately — in the original six g groups each have .05s spacing, so the hero is fully set within 2 seconds. Default is one sequence overall

use: <svg viewBox="0 0 2376 548" data-fx="sticker-float-drag" data-fx-sticker-float-drag="per: parent"><g><g data-fx-part="sticker"><circle …/></g> …</g> …</svg> — HTML element(<span data-fx-part="sticker">Also applies to )
note: The original uses framer-motion drag (dragSnapToOrigin, dragElastic .1, bounceStiffness 600, bounceDamping 20). The spring is a damped oscillation curve solved from the same mass, stiffness and damping, with the duration set to run until the amplitude falls below 1/1000. The artwork belongs to whoever uses it.
